input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes the MFN on us rather than in our favour: we must extend Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms given to any other technology supplier. It is open-ended — no defined product or service, no time limit, and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback (MFN confined to a defined product for 12 months with carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion of the Customer-side obligation; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere that would be affected.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the most-favoured-nation obligation in Section 7.2: our playbook does not permit an MFN running against us, and an open-ended commitment to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier is unworkable and inconsistent with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We remain happy to retain any MFN pricing granted in our favour.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2.
